newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexican peso closes firm as govt bond offer raised.
newsitem.headline: Mexican peso closes firm as govt bond offer raised.

text.p: The Mexican peso closed firmer against the dollar on Tuesday in an optimistic climate following an announcement that the government had decided to raise the amount of a new international placement of global bonds, traders said.
"The bond issue improves Mexico's image as a venue for foreign investment," a trader said.
"The absence of (dollar) buyers in the market contrasted with the inflow of some capital and supply by local brokers," a trader said.
The Mexican government earlier said it will increase its new bond placement from $750 million to $1 billion.
The benchmark 48-hour peso closed 1.2 centavos firmer at 7.5010/7.5050 per dollar and its 24-hour counterpart 1.3 centavos firmer at 7.4960/7.5010 per dollar.
Peso traders also said that several brokers decided to exercise dollar puts auctioned by Banco de Mexico at the end of August, which prevented the peso from gaining more strength against the dollar.

"As there was liquidity in the market and the opportunity cropped up to do a deal with Banco de Mexico at better prices (pesos for dollars), I think it's possible all puts were exercised," a trader said.
Traders estimated that the peso could remain firm on Wednesday, as long as the benchmark 28-day Cetes rate fell by less than 150 basis points at Tuesday night's primary auction.
